previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and CKD stage 3, was admitted for a nasal skin lesion concerning for MRSA infection. He had no systemic symptoms, and cultures were negative. He received IV vancomycin initially, then was switched to oral linezolid and Bactroban ointment for a 5-day course. Chemotherapy was held during the admission. He remained stable, with no fever or progression of infection, and was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics and follow up with oncology. His chronic conditions, including heart failure, diabetes, and anemia, remained stable.

EXAMINATION:  CT ORBIT, SELLA AND IAC W/O CONTRAST Q115 CT HEAD SUB

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with multiple myeloma presenting with fevers and
R eye swelling, rule out orbital cellulitis vs preseptal cellulitis.

TECHNIQUE:  Routine MDCT study of temporal bone was performed with coronal
reconstructions.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 4.6 s, 11.8 cm; CTDIvol = 117.7 mGy (Head) DLP =
1,301.0 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 2.4 s, 12.5 cm; CTDIvol = 33.4 mGy (Head) DLP = 426.9
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 1,728 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Brain MRI ___, noncontrast head CT ___

FINDINGS: 

Left : The external auditory canal is normal. The middle ear cavity is clear.
The ossicles and tegmen are intact.  There is no evidence for enlarged
vestibular aqueduct or superior semicircular canal dehiscence. The facial
nerve follows a normal course through the middle ear. There is no evidence for
inner ear dysplasia. The mastoids are clear.

Right: The external auditory canal is normal. There is opacification of the
right middle ear cavity and mastoid air cells, which appears grossly similar
to the prior MRI where it was noted to be intrinsically hyperintense on T1
weighted imaging, suggestive of inspissated mucus.  The ossicles and tegmen
are intact.  There is no evidence for enlarged vestibular aqueduct or superior
semicircular canal dehiscence. The facial nerve follows a normal course
through the middle ear. There is no evidence for inner ear dysplasia. The
mastoids are clear.

Orbits: There has been prior lens replacements bilaterally.  Mild right
proptosis.  There is soft tissue thickening and stranding about the right
orbit, which appears to be confined to the preseptal space, suggestive of
preseptal cellulitis.  Intraconal fat appears preserved.  Extra-ocular muscles
are within normal limits.  The left orbit is unremarkable.

Other: Limited evaluation of the brain parenchyma is notable for prominent
ventricles and sulci, likely due to age-related involutional changes. 
Intracranial carotid and vertebral artery calcifications noted.  There is
mucosal thickening of all visualized paranasal sinuses, without appreciable
air-fluid levels.


IMPRESSION:


1. Right preseptal cellulitis, without evidence of postseptal extension.
2. Chronic opacification of the right middle ear cavity and mastoid air cells,
with suggestion of chronic inspissated mucus on the prior MRI.
3. Paranasal sinus disease, worse compared to ___.

NOTIFICATION:   The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by ___
___, M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 10:40 am, 10 minutes after
discovery of the findings.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE BY EIA.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Negative results do not rule out B. burgdorferi infection.  Patients in early stages of infection or on antibiotic therapy may not produce  detectable levels of antibody

NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.
